title: A teddy bear for life
titleChinese: 为什么大人也爱泰迪熊？
paragraphs: One thing we always remember from our childhood is our favourite teddy bear. This soft, ragged toy was our comfort and companion. As we grow up, we normally give up our childish ways, and our furry friend often ends up in storage or at a jumble sale. But that’s not the case for everyone.

It seems that some grown-ups continue to need their cuddly toy by their sides. One sleep survey suggested a tenth of people in the UK need a teddy bear in bed. And for some adults, soft toys remain an essential presence – they take them wherever they go.

A cuddly toy can come in many forms – animals, strange shapes or just a piece of stuffed material. But it’s the teddy bear in particular that seems to have an enduring appeal – it gives us a nostalgic feeling and a reminder of our younger days. Writing for the BBC, historian David Cannadine says, “Perhaps it’s that bears represent the happy security of a childhood friend who never changes or lets you down.” For whatever reason, teddies appeal to both children and adults of all ages.

The teddy bear is much celebrated these days, and they’ve become something that we don’t just grow up with – people buy them as adults too. There are shops which sell only teddy bears, there are teddy bear museums in many countries, and teddy bear festivals regularly take place around the world.

While our soft toys offer us a kind of comfort blanket, some experts say it’s nothing to be ashamed of. It’s sometimes good to let go of the constraints of adult life and be a big kid again. And research commissioned by Barclaycard in the UK found 44% of adults have purchased playthings they enjoyed as children because they bring back happy memories. Colouring books, cuddly toys and board games were top of the list. So, if you’re still keeping your teddy a secret, don’t worry – you’re not alone!

vocabulary.entry: ragged /ˈræɡɪd/ adj. 破旧的；衣衫褴褛的
vocabulary.example: The old man wore a ragged jacket while walking in the park.
vocabulary.translation: 那位老人在公园里散步时穿着一件破旧的夹克。

vocabulary.entry: jumble sale /ˈdʒʌmbl seɪl/ 旧货义卖
vocabulary.example: We donated some old toys to the school jumble sale.
vocabulary.translation: 我们向学校的旧货义卖捐赠了一些旧玩具。

vocabulary.entry: cuddly /ˈkʌdli/ adj. 令人想拥抱的；毛茸茸的
vocabulary.example: The little girl fell asleep holding her cuddly teddy bear.
vocabulary.translation: 小女孩抱着她的毛绒泰迪熊睡着了。

vocabulary.entry: by one's sides /baɪ wʌnz saɪdz/ 在某人身边
vocabulary.example: Her pet cat stays by her sides whenever she feels lonely.
vocabulary.translation: 每当她感到孤独时，她的宠物猫就会陪在她身边。

vocabulary.entry: essential /ɪˈsenʃl/ adj. 极其重要的；必不可少的
vocabulary.example: A good diet is essential for maintaining a healthy body.
vocabulary.translation: 良好的饮食对维持身体健康至关重要。

vocabulary.entry: stuffed material /ˈstʌft məˈtɪəriəl/ 填充物
vocabulary.example: The cushion is filled with soft stuffed material for extra comfort.
vocabulary.translation: 这个靠垫填充了柔软的填充物，以增加舒适度。

vocabulary.entry: enduring /ɪnˈdjʊərɪŋ/ adj. 持久的；永恒的
vocabulary.example: The film has an enduring popularity among audiences of all ages.
vocabulary.translation: 这部电影在各个年龄段的观众中都经久不衰。

vocabulary.entry: nostalgic /nɒˈstældʒɪk/ adj. 怀旧的；乡愁的
vocabulary.example: Looking at old photos always makes me feel nostalgic for my childhood.
vocabulary.translation: 翻看旧照片总会让我对童年产生怀旧之情。

vocabulary.entry: let down /let daʊn/ 让……失望
vocabulary.example: I will never let down my friends who trust me so much.
vocabulary.translation: 我永远不会让如此信任我的朋友们失望。

vocabulary.entry: celebrate /ˈselɪbreɪt/ v. 赞美；推崇
vocabulary.example: The festival celebrates the rich cultural heritage of the region.
vocabulary.translation: 这个节日赞美该地区丰富的文化遗产。

vocabulary.entry: comfort blanket /ˈkʌmfət ˈblæŋkɪt/ 慰藉物；带来安慰的人或物
vocabulary.example: For many people, a favourite book is a comfort blanket in difficult times.
vocabulary.translation: 对很多人来说，一本心爱的书是困境中的慰藉物。

vocabulary.entry: ashamed /əˈʃeɪmd/ adj. 羞愧的；难为情的
vocabulary.example: She felt ashamed of forgetting her best friend's birthday.
vocabulary.translation: 她为忘记了闺蜜的生日而感到羞愧。

vocabulary.entry: constraints /kənˈstreɪnts/ n. 限制；约束
vocabulary.example: The team had to work within tight budget constraints to finish the project.
vocabulary.translation: 这个团队不得不在严格的预算限制下完成项目。

vocabulary.entry: let go of /let ɡəʊ ɒv/ 放下；释怀
vocabulary.example: It's important to let go of negative feelings and focus on the future.
vocabulary.translation: 放下负面情绪，专注于未来是很重要的。

vocabulary.entry: big kid /bɪɡ kɪd/ 童心未泯的成年人
vocabulary.example: My uncle is a big kid who still loves playing with toy cars.
vocabulary.translation: 我叔叔是个童心未泯的成年人，仍然喜欢玩玩具车。

vocabulary.entry: commission /kəˈmɪʃn/ v. 委托；授权
vocabulary.example: The government commissioned a survey on public transport satisfaction.
vocabulary.translation: 政府委托开展了一项关于公共交通满意度的调查。

vocabulary.entry: playthings /ˈpleɪθɪŋz/ n. 玩具；玩物
vocabulary.example: The attic is full of old playthings from my parents' childhood.
vocabulary.translation: 阁楼里装满了我父母童年时的旧玩具。

vocabulary.entry: bring back /brɪŋ bæk/ 使……回忆起；带回
vocabulary.example: The smell of freshly baked bread brings back memories of my grandma's kitchen.
vocabulary.translation: 新鲜出炉面包的香味让我回忆起奶奶的厨房。

vocabulary.entry: colouring book /ˈkʌlərɪŋ bʊk/ 涂色书
vocabulary.example: The kindergarten teacher gave each child a colouring book and some crayons.
vocabulary.translation: 幼儿园老师给每个孩子发了一本涂色书和一些蜡笔。

vocabulary.entry: board game /bɔːd ɡeɪm/ 桌面游戏；棋盘游戏
vocabulary.example: We spent the evening playing a board game with our neighbours.
vocabulary.translation: 我们晚上和邻居一起玩了桌面游戏。

vocabulary.entry: storage /ˈstɔːrɪdʒ/ n. 储存；储藏
vocabulary.example: We put the winter clothes in storage until the next year.
vocabulary.translation: 我们把冬衣存起来，留到明年再穿。

vocabulary.entry: appeal /əˈpiːl/ n. 吸引力；感染力
vocabulary.example: The small town's quiet charm has a special appeal to city dwellers.
vocabulary.translation: 这个小镇的宁静魅力对城市居民有着特殊的吸引力。

vocabulary.entry: security /sɪˈkjʊərəti/ n. 安全感；保障
vocabulary.example: Having a stable home gives children a sense of security.
vocabulary.translation: 拥有一个稳定的家能给孩子带来安全感。

vocabulary.entry: museum /mjuˈziːəm/ n. 专题博物馆
vocabulary.example: The toy museum has a large collection of vintage teddy bears.
vocabulary.translation: 这家玩具博物馆收藏了大量的老式泰迪熊。

vocabulary.entry: festival /ˈfestɪvl/ n. 主题活动；节庆
vocabulary.example: The local community holds a teddy bear festival every spring.
vocabulary.translation: 当地社区每年春天都会举办泰迪熊主题活动。

sentences.english: One thing we always remember from our childhood is our favourite teddy bear.
sentences.chinese: 童年里总有一样东西让我们念念不忘，那就是自己最心爱的泰迪熊。

sentences.english: This soft, ragged toy was our comfort and companion.
sentences.chinese: 这个柔软破旧的玩具曾是我们的慰藉与伙伴。

sentences.english: As we grow up, we normally give up our childish ways, and our furry friend often ends up in storage or at a jumble sale.
sentences.chinese: 长大后，我们通常会褪去稚气，而这个毛茸茸的小伙伴往往会被收进储物间，或是送去旧货义卖会。

sentences.english: But that’s not the case for everyone.
sentences.chinese: 但并非所有人都是如此。

sentences.english: It seems that some grown-ups continue to need their cuddly toy by their sides.
sentences.chinese: 有些成年人似乎依然需要毛绒玩具陪伴左右。

sentences.english: One sleep survey suggested a tenth of people in the UK need a teddy bear in bed.
sentences.chinese: 一项睡眠调查显示，英国有十分之一的人睡觉时必须抱着泰迪熊。

sentences.english: And for some adults, soft toys remain an essential presence – they take them wherever they go.
sentences.chinese: 对部分成年人而言，毛绒玩具是生活中不可或缺的存在——他们走到哪儿都会带着。

sentences.english: A cuddly toy can come in many forms – animals, strange shapes or just a piece of stuffed material.
sentences.chinese: 毛绒玩具的形态多种多样，有动物造型、奇趣形状，或是一块简单的填充布料。

sentences.english: But it’s the teddy bear in particular that seems to have an enduring appeal – it gives us a nostalgic feeling and a reminder of our younger days.
sentences.chinese: 但唯独泰迪熊似乎拥有经久不衰的吸引力——它能唤起我们的怀旧之情，让我们想起年少时光。

sentences.english: Writing for the BBC, historian David Cannadine says, “Perhaps it’s that bears represent the happy security of a childhood friend who never changes or lets you down.”
sentences.chinese: 历史学家大卫·坎纳丁在为BBC撰稿时表示：“或许是因为泰迪熊象征着童年玩伴那种永恒不变、永远不会让你失望的温暖安全感。”

sentences.english: For whatever reason, teddies appeal to both children and adults of all ages.
sentences.chinese: 无论出于何种原因，泰迪熊都深受各个年龄段的儿童与成年人的喜爱。

sentences.english: The teddy bear is much celebrated these days, and they’ve become something that we don’t just grow up with – people buy them as adults too.
sentences.chinese: 如今，泰迪熊早已成为备受追捧的存在，它不再只是我们童年的玩伴——成年人也会特意购买。

sentences.english: There are shops which sell only teddy bears, there are teddy bear museums in many countries, and teddy bear festivals regularly take place around the world.
sentences.chinese: 市面上有专门售卖泰迪熊的商店，许多国家建有泰迪熊博物馆，世界各地还会定期举办泰迪熊主题节日。

sentences.english: While our soft toys offer us a kind of comfort blanket, some experts say it’s nothing to be ashamed of.
sentences.chinese: 尽管毛绒玩具就像我们的“心灵慰藉毯”，但一些专家表示，这绝非什么丢人的事。

sentences.english: It’s sometimes good to let go of the constraints of adult life and be a big kid again.
sentences.chinese: 偶尔放下成年人的条条框框，重新做一回“大孩子”，其实是件好事。

sentences.english: And research commissioned by Barclaycard in the UK found 44% of adults have purchased playthings they enjoyed as children because they bring back happy memories.
sentences.chinese: 巴克莱卡公司在英国开展的一项研究发现，44%的成年人会购买童年时喜爱的玩具，因为这些玩具能勾起美好的回忆。

sentences.english: Colouring books, cuddly toys and board games were top of the list.
sentences.chinese: 填色书、毛绒玩具和桌面游戏高居榜单前列。

sentences.english: So, if you’re still keeping your teddy a secret, don’t worry – you’re not alone!
sentences.chinese: 所以，如果你还在偷偷珍藏着自己的泰迪熊，别担心——你绝对不是个例！
